proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 A_{2,n}=\left(\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{13/2}}\right)^{1/2},\quad
 A_{1,n}=\left(\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}\right)^{1/2},\quad
 A_{0,n}=\left(\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{5/2}}\right)^{1/2},
\]
and
\[
 B_{2,n}=h_n^{s-9/4},\qquad
 B_{1,n}=h_n^{s-5/4},\qquad
 B_{0,n}=h_n^{s-1/4}.
\]
Thus \(q_{2,n}=A_{2,n}+B_{2,n}\), \(q_{1,n}=A_{1,n}+B_{1,n}\), and \(q_{0,n}=A_{0,n}+B_{0,n}\).  Since \(h_n=n^{-a_h}\) and \(L_n=a_h\log n\),
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}h_n^{s-2}
 =\frac{n^{1/2-a_h(s-2)}}{\sqrt{a_h\log n}}.
\]
This tends to zero exactly when \(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\); equality is permitted by the logarithmic denominator.

The stochastic component of \(q_{2,n}\) is
\[
 A_{2,n}=(\log n)^{1/2}n^{-1/2+(13/4)a_h},
\]
which tends to zero exactly when \(a_h<2/13\).  The deterministic component \(B_{2,n}\) tends to zero for every \(a_h>0\), because \(s\geq8>9/4\).

Expanding the nonnegative product gives four terms.  The stochastic--stochastic term satisfies
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}A_{1,n}A_{0,n}
 =a_h^{-1/2}(\log n)^{1/2}n^{-1/2+(7/2)a_h},
\]
and therefore tends to zero exactly when \(a_h<1/7\).  The two mixed terms are
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}A_{1,n}B_{0,n}
 =a_h^{-1/2}h_n^{s-5/2},
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}B_{1,n}A_{0,n}
 =a_h^{-1/2}h_n^{s-5/2},
\]
so both vanish for \(a_h>0\) and \(s\geq8\).  Finally,
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}B_{1,n}B_{0,n}
 =\frac{n^{1/2-a_h(2s-3/2)}}{\sqrt{a_h\log n}},
\]
which tends to zero when \(a_h\geq1/(4s-3)\), equality again being allowed.  For \(s\geq8\),
\[
 \frac1{2(s-2)}>\frac1{4s-3},\qquad
 \frac17<\frac2{13},\qquad
 \frac1{2(s-2)}<\frac17.
\]
Intersecting the necessary and sufficient restrictions from the three displayed requirements yields exactly
\[
 \frac1{2(s-2)}\leq a_h<\frac17.
\]
Within this interval,
\[
 \frac{n h_n^7}{\log n}
 =\frac{n^{1-7a_h}}{\log n}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 \frac{n h_n^{13/2}}{\log n}
 =\frac{n^{1-(13/2)a_h}}{\log n}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
because \(a_h<1/7<2/13\), and
\[
 n h_n^2L_n^2=a_h^2n^{1-2a_h}(\log n)^2\longrightarrow\infty
\]
because \(a_h<1/7<1/2\).  This proves every assertion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume, in addition to the current hypotheses, the harmonic reduced-cost nondegeneracy condition.  For every \(P\in\mathcal F_s\) and every smooth four-density path with tangent \(\delta\), the selected lifted map \(P\mapsto(\widetilde T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\) is Fr\'echet differentiable.  Its derivative is the coupled scalar--harmonic operator \(\mathcal D_P\) in the corrected def:nested-derivative, and the identity \(B D^{-\mathsf T}=\alpha\mathsf C\) holds.  The inner and outer harmonic increments \(\dot a_p\) and \(\dot a_T\) are bounded cellwise Riesz functionals.  If \(u=(u_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) is a zero-integral density perturbation, the perturbed densities are positive, and \(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{2,1/4}}\) is sufficiently small, then the complete scalar--harmonic remainder satisfies
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}\left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j\right\rVert
 \leq C
 \left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}\right)
 \left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{0,1/4}}\right).
\]
Consequently the full harmonic score has uniformly bounded cellwise \(L^2(P_g)\) norm, contributes \(O(1/\log(1/h))\) to \(\Sigma_h(P)\), and has Green cross-covariance \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim omits the divergence responses induced by both harmonic increments and does not state the finite-dimensional transport-optimality equations that determine those increments. The replacement adds the genuinely necessary harmonic nondegeneracy hypothesis and states the corrected coupled derivative and mixed remainder.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Put \(e=e_{C1}-e_{C0}\).  For the inner problem, solve the scalar pushforward equation on the selected branch at a fixed harmonic coordinate \(a\), and denote its reduced intrinsic quadratic cost by \(\mathcal J_p(a)\).  At \(a=a_p\), transport optimality gives \(\nabla_a\mathcal J_p(a_p)=0\).  Let \(b_p=\dot a_p\) be determined by the differentiated finite-dimensional equation
\[
 \nabla_a^2\mathcal J_p(a_p)b_p
 +D_{(f_{C0},f_{C1})}\nabla_a\mathcal J_p(a_p)
       [\delta_{C0},\delta_{C1}]=0,
\]
and let the mean-zero pulled-back scalar increment \(u_p\) solve
\[
 \mathcal L_{\mathsf C}u_p
 =\Pi_0\!\left[e+\operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)\right].
\]
Thus the complete pulled-back inner differential is \(b_p+\nabla u_p\).  The pulled-back generated-target tangent entering the outer equation is
\[
 r_T=\alpha e+e_{T0}-e_{T1}
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}(b_p+\nabla u_p).
\]
For the outer problem, solve its scalar pushforward equation at fixed harmonic coordinate and denote the reduced cost by \(\mathcal J_T(a)\).  Let \(b_T=\dot a_T\) be determined by the differentiated equation
\[
 \nabla_a^2\mathcal J_T(a_T)b_T
 +D_{(f_{T1},q)}\nabla_a\mathcal J_T(a_T)
       [\delta_{T1},\dot q]=0,
\]
where
\[
 \dot q=p\#\delta_{T0}
 -\operatorname{div}\!\left(q\,(b_p+\nabla u_p)\circ p^{-1}\right),
\]
with the inner field interpreted before the pullback.  Let the mean-zero outer scalar increment \(u_T\) solve
\[
 \mathcal L_Bu_T=\Pi_0\!\left[r_T+\operatorname{div}(B b_T)\right].
\]
Define
\[
 \mathcal D_P[\delta]=(b_T+\nabla u_T)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 \mathcal D_P[\delta]=\mathcal H_P[\delta]
 +\left(
 \nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[\alpha e+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]
 -\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}
       \nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0 e]
 \right)_{\mathcal Y_J},
\]
where the full harmonic correction is
\[
 \mathcal H_P[\delta]=\left(
 b_T+\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
 \operatorname{div}(B b_T)
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}b_p
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}
 \nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
       \operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)
 \right]\right)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
proposed_definition_changes.reason: For nonconstant coefficients, the scalar mass equation for a variation with harmonic part also contains the divergence of the coefficient times that harmonic vector. The existing construction omits this term for both transports and therefore does not name the full derivative.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Pull the inner and generated-pushforward equations into treated-post coordinates using the corrected coupled scalar--harmonic derivative in def:nested-derivative.  Retain the entire correction \(\mathcal H_P\), including the scalar responses generated by \(\operatorname{div}(\mathsf C\dot a_p)\) and \(\operatorname{div}(B\dot a_T)\).  In a coordinate ball around each Green pole, decompose the periodic Green function into the Dirichlet Green function and an elliptic-harmonic correction; freeze \(B\) only inside the resulting energy parametrix.  Compare every nonlinearly transformed periodized kernel with its affine-coordinate version by Taylor expansion before applying Young's inequality.  Control coefficient and moving-pole errors in normalized \(L^2\), retain all within-cell generated-target cross products, and close the nested expansion with the mixed remainder
\[
 C\left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}\right)
  \left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{0,1/4}}\right)
\]
on a common small \(C^{2,1/4}\) neighborhood.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The analytic handle must start from the coupled scalar--harmonic derivative and the requested mixed high-times-low remainder; its current squared-high-norm and incomplete harmonic formulation is stale.

proposed_assumptions.condition: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\), for each of the inner transport \(p\) and the outer transport \(T\), the Hessian with respect to the two harmonic lift coordinates of the intrinsic quadratic transport cost, after the scalar pushforward equation has been solved on the selected no-cut branch, is positive definite and has smallest eigenvalue bounded below by a constant independent of \(P\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: Scalar ellipticity controls the mean-zero potential block, but uniqueness of each optimal map and separation from the lift boundary do not supply a uniform lower bound for the two-dimensional reduced-cost Hessian. That lower bound is required to solve the differentiated optimality equations uniformly and to obtain bounded harmonic Riesz scores.
proposed_assumptions.standard_or_novel: novel: uniform nondegeneracy of the reduced harmonic branch cost for both nested torus transports
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: The condition concerns only the finite-dimensional branch Hessians. It does not assume the Green covariance, score stability, Gaussian limit, adjoint consistency, coverage, or risk conclusion that the target results must prove.

In addition, the frozen derivative formula omits the scalar responses to the divergences of the nonconstant coefficients times those increments.

open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(F(x)=x+a+\nabla\phi(x)\) be either population transport on its no-cut branch, with source density \(f\), target density \(g\), Jacobian \(E_F=DF\), and scalar elliptic coefficient \(A_F=fE_F^{-1}\).  A path derivative has the Hodge form \(v=b+\nabla u\), where \(b=\dot a\) and \(\int_{\mathbb T^2}u=0\).  Differentiating
\[
 f(x)=g(F(x))\det E_F(x)
\]
and using the Piola identity for the cofactor of \(E_F\) gives
\[
 -\operatorname{div}\!\left(A_F(b+\nabla u)\right)
 =\det(E_F)\,\dot g\circ F-\dot f.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently the scalar equation is
\[
 \mathcal L_{A_F}u
 =\Pi_0\!\left[\det(E_F)\,\dot g\circ F-\dot f
 +\operatorname{div}(A_F b)\right].
\tag{2}
\]
Thus solving only \(\mathcal L_{A_F}u=\det(E_F)\dot g\circ F-\dot f\) omits \(\operatorname{div}(A_Fb)\) whenever \(A_F\) is nonconstant.

For the inner map, differentiating \(q=p\#P_{T0}\) gives the distributional identity
\[
 \dot q=p\#\delta_{T0}
 -\operatorname{div}\!\left(q\,(b_p+\nabla u_p)\circ p^{-1}\right).
\tag{3}
\]
After the change of variables \(R_0=p^{-1}\circ T\), equations (1)--(3) yield
\[
 \mathcal L_{\mathsf C}u_p
 =\Pi_0[e_{C1}-e_{C0}+\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p)]
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal L_Bu_T=\Pi_0\!\left[
 \alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}(b_p+\nabla u_p)
 +\operatorname{div}(Bb_T)\right].
\tag{5}
\]
Indeed, \(D=S(R_0)^{-1}H\), the population change-of-variables identities give \(f_{T1}=\alpha f_{C0}(R_0)\det D\), and direct multiplication gives
\[
 B D^{-\mathsf T}
 =f_{T1}H^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}
 =\alpha\det(D)D^{-1}A(R_0)D^{-\mathsf T}
 =\alpha\mathsf C.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (4)--(5) prove the corrected scalar propagation and show exactly which terms the frozen formula misses.

For fixed harmonic coordinate \(a\), the scalar equation is uniformly invertible on mean-zero periodic functions by ellipticity and Poincar\'e's inequality.  If \(\mathcal J_F(a)\) denotes the intrinsic quadratic transport cost after this scalar equation has been solved, the missing two equations are
\[
 \nabla_a\mathcal J_F(a_F)=0,
 \qquad
 \nabla_a^2\mathcal J_F(a_F)b
 +D_{(f,g)}\nabla_a\mathcal J_F(a_F)[\dot f,\dot g]=0.
\tag{7}
\]
The branch margin makes \(a_F\) an interior point, so the first equation in (7) is necessary.  Pointwise uniqueness of the optimal map does not imply a uniform positive lower bound for the Hessian in the second equation.  Such a bound is exactly what is needed to invert the finite-dimensional block uniformly and to represent \(b_p\) and \(b_T\) by uniformly bounded cellwise Riesz scores.

open_obligations.partial_result:
The deterministic energy-parametrix calculation can be carried out without subtracting two non-energy functions.  In a coordinate ball about \(y\), let
\[
 \Gamma_y(z)=-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B(y)}}
 \log\lvert B(y)^{-1/2}(z-y)\rvert
\]
and let \(\chi\) be supported in that ball and equal to one near \(y\).  The residual divergence field is
\[
 F_y(z)=(B(z)-B(y))\chi(z)\nabla\Gamma_y(z).
\]
Uniform \(C^{0,1/4}\) control of \(B\) and \(\lvert\nabla\Gamma_y(z)\rvert\leq C\lvert z-y\rvert^{-1}\) imply
\[
 \lvert F_y(z)\rvert\leq C\lvert z-y\rvert^{-3/4},
 \qquad
 \int_{\lvert z-y\rvert<r}\lvert F_y(z)\rvert^2\,dz
 \leq C\int_0^r t^{-1/2}\,dt<\infty.
\tag{8}
\]
After adding the smooth cutoff terms and subtracting their mean, Lax--Milgram on the mean-zero periodic energy space constructs a residual \(w_y\) before any testing.  Coercivity and Poincar\'e's inequality then give
\[
 \lVert\nabla w_y\rVert_{L^2(\mathbb T^2)}
 \leq C\bigl(\lVert F_y\rVert_2+1\bigr)\leq C.
\tag{9}
\]
For the torus pointwise Green bound, one must first write the periodic Green function in a coordinate ball as the corresponding Dirichlet Green function plus an elliptic-harmonic correction.  The bounded-domain interior gradient estimate applies only to the Dirichlet term; interior estimates bound the correction, and compactness controls the complement of a smaller ball.  This yields the required torus reduction but does not provide the missing harmonic reduced-cost Hessian.

Equations (8)--(9) show that the frozen fundamental solution has an \(L^2\)-bounded energy remainder.  They do not by themselves establish the nonlinear-coordinate kernel Taylor remainder, the \(o(h_n)\) moving-pole estimate, the opposite-fold score comparison, or the two-endpoint generated-target remainder.  Those estimates must be proved after the coupled scalar--harmonic derivative is well posed; Young's inequality can then transport an already established \(L^2\) kernel remainder but cannot create it.

open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditionally on a valid coupled derivative and the uniform energy-parametrix bounds, the logarithmic coefficient is forced algebraically.  The frozen fundamental solution for \(-\operatorname{div}(B(y_j)\nabla\cdot)\) satisfies
\[
 \int_{h<\lvert z-y_j\rvert<r_0}
 \nabla\Gamma_{B(y_j)}(z-y_j)
 \nabla\Gamma_{B(y_j)}(z-y_j)^{\mathsf T}\,dz
 =\frac{B(y_j)^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B(y_j)}}\log(1/h)+O(1).
\tag{10}
\]
At the pole, each treated-cell transformed noise has intensity \(f_{T1}(y_j)\).  Each control-cell transformed noise has intensity
\[
 f_{C0}(R_0(y_j))\det D(y_j)
 =\frac{f_{T1}(y_j)}{\alpha(y_j)},
\]
and its leading coefficient is \(\alpha(y_j)\); hence its variance intensity is \(\alpha(y_j)f_{T1}(y_j)\).  Since \(B=f_{T1}H^{-1}\), multiplying (10) by these intensities and the four sample-size factors gives
\[
 V_j=\left\{\alpha(y_j)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})
 +\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\right\}
 \frac{\sqrt{\det H(y_j)}H(y_j)}{4\pi f_{T1}(y_j)}.
\tag{11}
\]
Independence adds the four cell covariances, while separated poles make off-diagonal grid blocks only \(O(1)\) before division by \(\log(1/h)\).  Formula (11) is therefore the only possible limiting block.  The unresolved step is the uniform replacement of the complete coupled scores by these frozen responses, including their within-control-cell cross terms.

open_obligations.partial_result:
For the cross-fitted multiplier score, conditioning on the training folds makes the evaluation-fold observations independent.  For every matrix entry, the fourth-moment envelope would give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left[
 L_n^{-1}\frac n{n_g}\frac1{n_g}
 \sum_{i=1}^{n_g}
 \widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r(i))}(X_{g,i})
 \widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r(i))}(X_{g,i})^{\mathsf T}
 \ \middle|\ \text{training folds}\right]
 \leq \frac{C}{n h_n^2L_n^2}=o(1).
\tag{13}
\]
Moreover, if
\[
 L_n^{-1/2}\lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz makes the normalized difference between pilot and population second moments \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).  Fold centering is also negligible.  Equations (13) and the score comparison would reduce \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}\) to \(\Sigma_{h_n}(P)\).  The unresolved ingredient is precisely that score comparison for the corrected harmonic and moving-pole terms.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Transfer an established joint critical limit and consistent covariance estimate through the conditional multiplier maximum law.
open_obligations.obstruction: Both probabilistic parent results remain open after the harmonic audit, so coverage cannot presently be asserted even though the ridge totalizes every finite sample.
open_obligations.attempted: The conditional Gaussian law of the multiplier and the parameter-free continuous limiting maximum of independent blockwise chi-square variables were derived.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditionally on the data, the Gaussian multipliers give the exact identity
\[
 Z^\star\mid\text{data}\sim N(0,\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}).
\tag{14}
\]
If the joint critical limit and covariance consistency were established, the ridge \(\theta_n I_{2J}\) would vanish in operator norm, and (14) would converge conditionally to \(N(0,V(P))\).  Because \(V(P)\) is block diagonal and every \(V_j(P)\) is positive definite, the limiting statistic is
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}Z_j^{\mathsf T}V_j(P)^{-1}Z_j
 \ \stackrel{d}{=}\ \max_{1\leq j\leq J}Q_j,
 \qquad Q_1,\ldots,Q_J\ \text{independent }\chi_2^2.
\tag{15}
\]
Its distribution is continuous and parameter free, so conditional quantile convergence plus the joint central limit theorem would yield simultaneous coverage \(1-\gamma\).  The ridge already guarantees finite-sample invertibility.  Coverage remains open because neither parent convergence is presently established.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the class-uniform upper second-moment bound for the specified plug-in under the corrected coupled expansion.
open_obligations.obstruction: The established Green alternatives prove the local lower rate, but the upper bound requires integrated control of the unresolved mixed nonlinear remainder and bounded fallback event. Weak convergence would not suffice.
open_obligations.attempted: The two-point Hellinger testing argument was completed from the established alternatives, and the upper bound was reduced to the mixed expansion and its tail moments.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The lower half of the risk claim follows from the already established Green alternatives.  Let
\[
 \Delta_n=\left\lvert\upsilon^{\mathsf T}
 \{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right\rvert.
\]
The established separation and \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=(\eta/a_h)L_n\) give
\[
 \Delta_n^2\geq c(P_0)\zeta^2\frac{L_n}{n}.
\tag{16}
\]
For any estimator, testing according to which of the two scalar parameters is closer shows
\[
 \max_{\sigma\in\{+,-\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_{n,\sigma}}\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P_{n,\sigma})\rVert^2
 \geq \frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}
 \left(1-\operatorname{TV}(P_{n,+}^{\otimes},P_{n,-}^{\otimes})\right).
\tag{17}
\]
The established product-Hellinger bound is at most \(1/2\); choosing the fixed amplitude smaller if necessary bounds the total variation in (17) strictly below one.  Equations (16)--(17) prove a positive lower constant after multiplication by \(n/L_n\).  The class-uniform upper bound is still open because it needs the coupled mixed stochastic expansion and its integrated-tail control; weak convergence alone cannot supply the required second moment.

prose_updates.tldr: The note proves intrinsic torus changes-in-changes identification, the bandwidth arithmetic, and the fixed-center Green-aligned local lower bound. A new audit shows that the selected-lift derivative must couple each scalar Monge--Ampere equation to a two-dimensional transport-optimality equation. The frozen assumptions do not provide uniform nondegeneracy of those harmonic blocks, so the variable-coefficient covariance, Gaussian limit, adjoint covariance, ellipses, and uniform upper risk remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-path and uniform-law transport results do not provide either the finite-dimensional selected-harmonic derivative for a nested torus transport or the shrinking-bandwidth variable-coefficient Green control. The frozen scalar mass equations alone do not determine the harmonic increments.
project_justification.niche: The corrected architecture separates two finite-dimensional transport-optimality blocks from the scalar elliptic Green responses and retains all four cell noises and generated-target cross terms. Algebra fixes the candidate logarithmic covariance, but only after uniform harmonic invertibility and score stability are proved can it become an inference theorem.
project_justification.fill: The note currently supplies identification, the exact scalar propagation showing the omitted harmonic-divergence terms, a proposed uniform reduced-cost Hessian condition, the sharp mixed bandwidth calculation, the fixed-center lower-bound experiment, and conditional reductions for covariance, Gaussian approximation, adjoint estimation, coverage, and risk. It does not claim those conditional results as proved.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the order-s signed periodized KDE followed by clipping and mass normalization. The proposed covariance algorithm is two-fold cross-fitted and retains harmonic scores and generated-target cross products, but its consistency awaits a valid coupled scalar--harmonic derivative and uniform moving-pole score bounds. The ridge still guarantees finite-sample block invertibility.

prose_updates.related_work: The Euclidean multivariate changes-in-changes paper motivates identification, while the present core separately proves its intrinsic torus identification lemma. The available fixed-path linearization does not determine or uniformly control the torus harmonic branch coordinates, and the published dimension-two Gaussian result covers only its stated uniform fixed-source case. Neither source closes the nested variable-coefficient harmonic or shrinking-bandwidth problem isolated here.
prose_updates.interpretation: At a prespecified treated-post location, the target remains the translation-aware no-treatment displacement. The four-cell expression with control weight \(\alpha\) and both treated-cell contributions is now an algebraically derived candidate covariance: it follows from local transformed-noise intensities, but its use for uncertainty quantification is conditional on the coupled harmonic and uniform Green estimates.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The first unresolved layer is finite dimensional: pointwise uniqueness and lift-branch separation do not imply a class-uniform lower bound for the reduced transport-cost Hessian in the harmonic coordinates. After that condition is resolved, the analysis must still prove the torus energy parametrix, nonlinear-versus-affine transformed-kernel remainder, moving-pole rate, opposite-fold score stability, fourth moments, and the two-endpoint mixed nested remainder. The broader upper bandwidth endpoint is not adopted while these steps remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established results cover intrinsic torus identification, bandwidth arithmetic, and a fixed-center logarithmic local lower bound under smooth positive four-cell sampling. No Gaussian approximation, feasible covariance theorem, simultaneous ellipse coverage, or class-uniform plug-in upper risk is presently claimed. Applying the proposal to a Card--Krueger bivariate reanalysis additionally requires a prespecified smooth periodic outcome construction, a defensible independent-cell approximation, approval or proof of harmonic branch nondegeneracy, and numerical errors below the eventual statistical scales.
